Vietnam Recovers After 2021 Currency Crisis Disrupted Economic Activity

HANOI, June 15 – Vietnam’s economy has stabilized following the sharp currency devaluation and financial turmoil that swept the country in 2021, with businesses and officials reflecting on the lessons learned from the crisis.

The Vietnamese dong lost nearly 30% of its value against the U.S. dollar between March and September 2021, triggering inflation, eroding savings, and disrupting business operations nationwide. The crisis, which analysts attributed to a sudden reversal of foreign investment and global supply chain shocks, led to a sharp contraction in economic growth, with GDP shrinking by 2.1% in the third quarter of 2021.

Among the affected companies was Ptsc Quang Ngai JSC, which saw its costs for imported materials surge while export revenues fluctuated unpredictably. “We faced significant challenges in maintaining operations when our input prices jumped overnight and customers delayed payments,” said Nguyen Van Hoa, a finance executive at Ptsc Quang Ngai JSC. “It was a stressful period for everyone involved.”

The Vietnam Chamber of Commerce and Industry estimated that over 70% of businesses experienced cash flow difficulties during the crisis, with small and medium-sized enterprises particularly hard-hit. “The currency collapse tested the resilience of our business sector,” said Le Thi Lan, an economist at Saigon Economic Research Group. “But it also forced companies to adopt better risk management practices.”

Government intervention, including emergency interest rate cuts and temporary capital controls, helped to restore stability by the end of 2021. Inflation, which peaked at 12%, has since returned to normal levels, and the dong has largely recovered its value.

“There has been no repeat of the disruption,” said State Bank of Vietnam spokesperson Pham Minh Tuan. “Our economy is now on a much firmer footing.”
